title: observability: token-level metrics, tracing, and logging dashboards + alert tuning
author: Priya Shah
description:
Context: production customers have been asking for clearer token-level cost and latency visibility tied to KV-cache behavior and per-route tracing. Alerts were firing too often for noisy but non-actionable token-cost skews. This PR adds combined metrics, tracing spans, and structured logging hooks plus new dashboards and tuned alerting thresholds to reduce noise while preserving SLO coverage.

What this PR does: adds token-level metrics (cost_per_token, tokens_generated, tokens_cached_hit_rate), KV cache hit/miss breakdown per-model and per-route, standardized tracing spans for request->batch->infer->emit, structured log fields for token_cost and kv_state, Grafana dashboards with prebuilt panels and drilldown links, and alert rule changes tuned against realistic traffic profiles.

Checklist: - [x] Metrics emitted from serving runtime (prometheus counters/gauges) - [x] Tracing spans instrumented (opentelemetry) for key phases - [x] Structured logging hooks added to emitter and fallback paths - [x] Grafana dashboard JSONs added and tested against staging data - [x] Alert rules adjusted: reduced false positives, added multi-window evaluation and increased thresholds for low-volume routes - [x] Docs updated with dashboard screenshots and runbook summary - [x] Backfill migration script included for historic tokens_cost aggregation (lightweight)

Notes on approach: We prioritized label dimensions that are high-cardinality but necessary for debugging: model, route, tenant_id (limited cardinality via hashed buckets in metrics), cache_state (hit|miss|partial), and batch_size_bucket. To avoid cardinality explosion, the exporter aggregates tenant_id into 100 buckets for charts and keeps exact tenant_id only in traces/logs for on-demand debugging. Alert rules use the aggregated buckets.

Testing and verification: unit tests for metric name/label invariants added, integration run in perf-canary with 48h of synthetic traffic to validate alert rates, end-to-end tracing validated in staging with Jaeger. CI: lint, unit, integration passed after two reruns (flaky test fixed).

Rollout plan: staged rollout by region and capacity tier: start with staging -> us-west-hosted -> eu-hosted -> dedicated pools. Monitor alert rate and token-cost deltas for 72 hours per region. Immediate rollback plan: revert feature flag and remove alert rules if token-cost anomalies exceed 5x baseline or SLOs degrade.

Related: Linear ENG-4523 for dashboard work, SRE-213 for alert tuning guide. Refer to docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/observability/token-metrics and runbook at https://linear.app/redwood/issue/SRE-213/runbook

d4e5f6a - runtime: emit token-level counters and cache_state labels
f7a8b9c - tracing: add spans for request->batch->infer->emit and propagate trace_id
a1b2c3d - logging: structured log fields for token_cost and kv_state, improved formatter
b2c3d4e - alerts: adjust thresholds and add multi-window evaluation; add mute windows for low-volume routes
c3d4e5f - tests/docs: add unit tests and docs updates, include backfill script
review_comments: Evan Carter requested changes: limit tenant_id label cardinality to 100 buckets to avoid TSDB blowup; please document bucketing logic. - Author reply: implemented bucketing in metrics_emitter.go and added doc section explaining tradeoffs.
Marta Kovač asked to include a low-volume mute window on alerts and multi-window evaluation to avoid morning spikes; Author: added 15m/1h/6h windows with majority-vote logic.
Daniel Kim flagged potential performance overhead in tracing; Author: added sampling at 1% by default and 100% for error/alerted requests; added unit tests for trace propagation.
Security review (internal): ensure tenant_id hashing is irreversible; Author: using SHA256 with a salt from KMS, documented in telemetry exporter code comments.
ci_checks: integration-tests: pass (2 reruns due to flaky db-cleanup test, fixed)
release_notes: Add token-level cost/latency observability including dashboards, tracing spans, and tuned alerting. Reduces alert noise and provides drilldowns for KV cache behavior. Rollout controlled by feature flag; staged rollout recommended.
notes_for_ops: Staged rollout required. Watch alert burn rate metrics and token_cost/{bucket} deltas. If alerts spike, disable new alert rules and toggle feature flag 'obs_token_metrics_v1'. Backfill script provided for retrospective analysis.
